factions.name: The Lantern Concord
factions.origin: Clergy, lay wardens and refuge keepers who protected evacuation shelters after Emergence Day.
factions.purpose: Keep living people alive; hold thresholds, tend the harmed and lead cleansing rites.

factions.name: The Meridian Survey
factions.origin: Surviving surveyors, engineers, emergency radio crews and civilian researchers who mapped routes through the lost districts.
factions.purpose: Measure the danger, preserve reliable testimony and prove that a road or building can be reclaimed.

factions.name: The Ashen Collegium
factions.origin: Occult scholars and survivors of failed bargains who pooled dangerous knowledge after the old institutions collapsed.
factions.purpose: Find and sever supernatural claims on the living; controlled contact is a means to removal, never worship.

sites.title: The Briar House
sites.emergence: A family shelter closed its doors during the first attacks.
sites.survival: Neighbours shared a cellar refuge before evacuation.
sites.trace: A late-2022 shelter card tucked into older family correspondence.

sites.title: Hollowmere Farm
sites.emergence: Road refugees reached the farm as transport failed.
sites.survival: Growers and Lantern wardens kept a ration and wash rota.
sites.trace: A seed ledger, bed-allocation list and later safe-route correction.

sites.title: Ravenshade School
sites.emergence: Classrooms became an emergency reception point.
sites.survival: Volunteer crews kept names and departure routes as halls were lost.
sites.trace: An evacuation register with a later Meridian verification slip.

sites.title: Blackthorn Manor
sites.emergence: Private gates shut while the district sought shelter.
sites.survival: Survivors later reopened one service wing as a shelter.
sites.trace: Contradictory gate logs, communal cooking and repaired locks.

sites.title: Beckenburg Penitentiary
sites.emergence: Staff and prisoners faced the same supernatural assault.
sites.survival: An improvised evacuation crossed former security boundaries.
sites.trace: A joint headcount and keys tied to an evacuation route, without treating prisoners as monsters.

sites.title: St. Dymphna Hospital
sites.emergence: Care and transport failed during Emergence Day.
sites.survival: Patients and staff built a protected ward before evacuating.
sites.trace: A continuity-of-care list, mobility aids and a later rescue annotation; illness is never the haunting's cause.

sites.title: St. Alban Academy
sites.emergence: The academy's old assumptions failed in the first attacks.
sites.survival: Researchers joined the Ashen Collegium to test and unbind dangerous claims.
sites.trace: Crossed-out theories, a failed seal and a later safe procedure.

sites.title: Beckenburg College
sites.emergence: Student buildings became temporary aid stations.
sites.survival: Engineering and radio volunteers helped form Meridian field crews.
sites.trace: A hand-built route board and a repaired receiver beside older coursework.

sites.title: St. Brigid Parish
sites.emergence: The church sheltered people whose beliefs did not protect them from the attacks.
sites.survival: Refuge keepers helped establish the Lantern Concord.
sites.trace: A shared shelter register and a repaired ward threshold; belief alone never guarantees safety.

sites.title: Blackpine Logging Camp
sites.emergence: The camp was already closed when the supernatural returned in late 2022.
sites.survival: Displaced survivors used one logging cabin in 2025; a caretaker later recorded their traces.
sites.trace: Pre-Emergence payroll discrepancy, later shelter journal and maintenance sheet are separate layers.

sites.title: Camp Hollow Creek
sites.emergence: Holiday shelters became a stranded convoy's refuge.
sites.survival: Survivors moved between shore and washhouse as routes failed.
sites.trace: Camp maps overwritten with refuge counts, repaired cooking gear and later route markers.

sites.title: Red Mesa Ancestral Caves
sites.emergence: Modern travellers were stranded by the wider catastrophe.
sites.survival: Rescue teams followed local guidance and documented safe passages.
sites.trace: Modern emergency ropes and dated survey tags, explicitly separate from ancestral markings or cultural blame.

sites.title: Widow's Peak Fire Lookout
sites.emergence: The lookout relayed reports as the forests and roads became unsafe.
sites.survival: A radio keeper maintained a signal for travelling survivors.
sites.trace: Weather records interrupted by an emergency frequency list and later Meridian bearings.

sites.title: Dead Man's Claim
sites.emergence: Dormant workings were unsafe again after Emergence Day.
sites.survival: A rescue party attempted a measured return, leaving checked retreat markers.
sites.trace: Old assay/payroll dates and new rescue tallies; links to Blackpine remain provisional.

sites.title: Drowned Fisherman's Wharf
sites.emergence: Boats carried refugees when land routes broke.
sites.survival: Crews rationed fuel and repeated rescue crossings.
sites.trace: Passenger lists, patched moorings and a later warning against an unsafe berth.

sites.title: Saint Bartholomew's Forgotten Cemetery
sites.emergence: The dead returned to a place already used for remembrance.
sites.survival: Survivors recorded missing people without assuming every missing person was dead.
sites.trace: A memorial ledger, temporary ward posts and named rescue searches.

sites.title: Northwatch Research Station
sites.emergence: The remote station lost contact during the first attacks.
sites.survival: A skeleton crew rationed heat and attempted to re-establish a safe link.
sites.trace: Fuel and radio logs distinguish equipment failure from reported supernatural events.

sites.title: Blackwater Hydroelectric Dam
sites.emergence: Power loss and supernatural danger disrupted evacuation.
sites.survival: Maintenance crews risked limited returns to restore civilian supply.
sites.trace: Isolation tags, rationed work lamps and a later restart checklist.

sites.title: Monastery of Ashen Bells
sites.emergence: A refuge bell sounded across the first lost settlements.
sites.survival: Shelter keepers disagreed over sealing the doors or admitting more people.
sites.trace: A disputed admissions ledger and a later Concord relief list; no automatic religious guilt.

sites.title: Mourning Marsh
sites.emergence: Flooded routes divided fleeing households.
sites.survival: Survivors maintained raised trails and passed refuge markers onward.
sites.trace: Boot repairs, water-level marks and a later rescue line above older fishing traces.

sites.title: Gallows Pass Railway
sites.emergence: Emergency trains carried people away from the first attacks.
sites.survival: Rail crews kept a vulnerable evacuation and supply corridor open.
sites.trace: A departure manifest, improvised signals and later track-clearance stamps.

sites.title: Greywater Cannery
sites.emergence: Workers opened stores to a hungry district during the collapse.
sites.survival: Survivors rationed food while attempting to restore the coastal supply chain.
sites.trace: Production labels beneath relief tallies and a later reclamation inspection.

sites.title: Castle Beckenburg
sites.emergence: The castle became a defensible refuge during the collapse.
sites.survival: Survivors of three major factions made it a shared reclamation headquarters.
sites.trace: The Common Archive keeps testimony, corrections, missing names and records of places made safe.

pages.title: Matthis Rook / Keeper of the Common Archive
paragraphs: I kept parish and council records before I kept the names of the missing. The castle took me in when there was nowhere left to carry the boxes.
We do not clear a house to add a monster to a book. We clear it so a family can sleep there again. The Beckenburg Project exists to make ordinary life possible.
Ask what a record can prove, who wrote it, and what they could not see. I am a witness and an archivist, not an oracle.

pages.title: Emergence Day / late 2022
paragraphs: Supernatural forces that had lain dormant re-emerged in late 2022. Survivors call the catastrophe Emergence Day. The dead and other hostile forces took violent, bloody retribution upon the living.
Homes, roads and places of refuge were lost. Conflicting local accounts record the collapse; the archive does not invent a single precise date, a proven cause or a shared motive for every entity.
What is certain is the human cost. Missing lists, evacuation marks and interrupted work survive in the places we return to.

pages.title: The long return / the Beckenburg Project
paragraphs: Over many grueling years, humanity has fought to regain its place in a world occupied by the dead. Refuge networks became supply routes; supply routes became the first reclaimed districts.

Castle Beckenburg holds a coalition whose purpose is to remove supernatural threats and make places safe for normal people. Naming a ghost is useful only when that knowledge helps us survive, sever its hold and finish the work.
A return inspection matters as much as a victory report. The living must be able to use the place afterward.

pages.title: A life carried in record boxes
paragraphs: Matthis Rook was already an elderly municipal archivist when Emergence Day came. He helped neighbours carry copied registers through a failed evacuation; the originals and several people were lost.
His daughter Mara is listed as missing. He refuses to turn uncertainty into a death certificate. A hand tremor, repaired spectacles and a walking cane make patient work necessary.

He maintains the Common Archive in the castle's east records wing. Factions supply testimony and shelter staff help him catalogue it. His counsel, records and portrait are available here; he is not a recruitable field ally.

pages.title: Reading a reclaimed place
paragraphs: First distinguish what was here before late 2022, what happened during Emergence Day, and what survivors changed in the years afterward. A closed mill can contain new bedding; an old school can contain a later evacuation register.
Look for heat, water, light, food, repairs and a way out. These tell us how people stayed alive. A document is testimony, not automatic proof of the current entity or a completed mission.
The site ledger follows. Several locations remain proposals; their archive notes describe planned story threads rather than completed expeditions.
